correctness.rationale: The exact normalized determinant follows from a confluent Vandermonde identity and is independently reconstructed in verify.py. Angular uniqueness follows from Hadamard equality and Newton identities; strict radial uniqueness from positive variance of two truncated exponential families; the full singular spectrum from 2x2 Fourier blocks; the e*4^(-n) limit from exponentially accurate Poisson truncation and a locally quadratic log determinant. The exact hypotheses n>=2, t>0 and fixed common-circle geometry are explicit. The code passes 45 finite checks but is not used as a proof of asymptotics.

value.rationale: The natural objective is the information-volume determinant of n value/derivative pairs normalized by their actual finite Fock functional norms, compared with 2n distinct equally normalized value samples. The sharp asymptotic e*4^(-n) reveals an exponential co-location loss in the best designs, alongside unique design radii, angular rigidity, and all singular values. This is more than a routine cardinality or normalization observation and is relevant to stable spectral sampling design.
